parts.name: Segment I (caudate lobe)
parts.info: Sits at the back, wrapped around the inferior vena cava. It drains straight into the vena cava. Each Couinaud segment has its own blood supply and bile drainage, so surgeons can remove one on its own.
parts.fact: Because of its separate drainage, the caudate lobe often grows larger when the rest of the liver is scarred.

parts.name: Segment II
parts.info: Upper part of the left lateral section. Each Couinaud segment has its own blood supply and bile drainage, so surgeons can remove one on its own.
parts.fact: Segments II and III are often used for living-donor transplants to children.

parts.name: Segment III
parts.info: Lower part of the left lateral section, near the falciform ligament. Each Couinaud segment has its own blood supply and bile drainage, so surgeons can remove one on its own.
parts.fact: Together with segment II it forms the classic 'left lateral section'.

parts.name: Segment IV
parts.info: The medial part of the left liver, beside the gallbladder bed. Each Couinaud segment has its own blood supply and bile drainage, so surgeons can remove one on its own.
parts.fact: Also called the quadrate lobe on its underside.

parts.name: Segment V
parts.info: Front-lower part of the right liver. The gallbladder sits beneath it. Each Couinaud segment has its own blood supply and bile drainage, so surgeons can remove one on its own.
parts.fact: Segments IV and V are removed with the gallbladder in some cancer operations.

parts.name: Segment VI
parts.info: Back-lower part of the right liver. Each Couinaud segment has its own blood supply and bile drainage, so surgeons can remove one on its own.
parts.fact: It touches the right kidney below.

parts.name: Segment VII
parts.info: Back-upper part of the right liver, under the diaphragm. Each Couinaud segment has its own blood supply and bile drainage, so surgeons can remove one on its own.
parts.fact: Liver biopsies are often taken from segments VI and VII through the ribs.

parts.name: Segment VIII
parts.info: Front-upper part of the right liver, under the dome of the diaphragm. Each Couinaud segment has its own blood supply and bile drainage, so surgeons can remove one on its own.
parts.fact: Tumours here can be hard to reach because it sits high under the ribs and the diaphragm.

parts.name: Hepatic veins
parts.info: Three main veins that drain filtered blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava. They mark the borders between segments.
parts.fact: The right, middle and left hepatic veins divide the liver into four vertical sections.

parts.name: Portal vein
parts.info: Brings nutrient-rich blood from the gut and spleen. It supplies about 75% of the liver's blood.
parts.fact: Shown in purple: its blood is low in oxygen but full of absorbed nutrients.

parts.name: Hepatic artery
parts.info: Supplies oxygen-rich blood, about 25% of the liver's flow.
parts.fact: The bile ducts depend on the hepatic artery for their blood supply.

parts.name: Bile ducts
parts.info: Collect bile made by liver cells and carry it to the gallbladder and the intestine.
parts.fact: The liver makes roughly 500–1000 ml of bile a day.

parts.name: Gallbladder
parts.info: A pear-shaped pouch under the liver that stores and concentrates bile, then squeezes it out after a fatty meal.
parts.fact: It holds about 30–50 ml and can concentrate bile up to ten times.

parts.name: Inferior vena cava
parts.info: The large vein running behind the liver, receiving the hepatic veins on its way to the heart.
parts.fact: Part of it is embedded in a groove on the back of the liver.
